title: Either branch operations and conditional callback composition
explanation: In the value model, left_or_default/right_or_default return the matching payload independently of the Default computation. On the opposite variant they delegate its exact modeled outcome. Separate theorems describe its returned value only under a normal-result premise and propagate modeled failure/divergence only under the corresponding premise. No particular Default value, failure freedom or termination is certified. The handwritten conversions between Result<R,L> and Either<L,R> preserve each payload: Result Ok becomes Either Right and Result Err becomes Either Left; the reverse maps Right to Ok and Left to Err. Every variant returns normally in the model, and both composition orders reconstruct the original value. The foreign self of the reverse implementation is core::result::Result<R,L>, not Either. Twelve callback APIs compose a supplied mathematical callback contract with variant selection. is_left_and/right_and apply the callback only to the indicated variant and otherwise return false; is_left_or/right_or return true on the indicated variant and apply the callback to the other. map_left/right map only the named payload and preserve the other variant and payload. map_left_or/right_or return the mapped named payload or the supplied default. left_or_else/right_or_else preserve the named payload or compute it from the opposite payload. left_and_then/right_and_then return the selected callback-produced Either unchanged, or preserve the opposite variant and payload. IntoEither::into_either chooses Left on true and Right on false, preserving the payload. IntoEither::into_either_with applies the predicate to the modeled borrowed payload and selects that branch from its mathematical result. The original impl<T> IntoEither for T has no overrides: its compiler-extracted dictionary is linked directly to the verified default, removing an extra dispatch assumption. Selected predicate failure propagates unchanged. The twelve inherent callback APIs use a normal-result premise for every callback argument; the IntoEither predicate theorem needs it only at the actual input. Separate companion theorems show selected callback failure is propagated unchanged and non-selected branches preserve their result without any callback success premise. For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the following value-semantic guarantees exclude payload destructor effects; they do not establish Rust panic freedom for arbitrary Drop implementations. In that model, is_left/is_right identify the actual branch; left/right return the corresponding optional payload; left_or/right_or select that payload or the given default; flip swaps the branch and a separate composition theorem proves flipping twice returns the original value. left_and/right_and select the supplied value or preserve the opposite payload. factor_none moves the optional payload outside Either while retaining its tag. factor_first/factor_second move the common tuple component outside Either. as_ref preserves the variant and referenced value; as_mut preserves the initial view and its generated backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back to the original variant. The earlier thirty named bodies return normally in the value model under their stated conditions. The two default-fallback methods instead retain the entire abstract Default outcome on the fallback branch; they can model-fail or model-diverge when that supplied computation does. Their matching-payload branch returns the payload without any Default success premise.
trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are assumed; callback behavior is an explicit premise of the conditional composition theorems. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value and backward-function semantics; they do not independently verify the compiler borrow checker or Rust aliasing model.
environment: Original crates.io either 1.19.0 Rust files and Cargo.toml, archive-compared; default features, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Rust nightly-2026-09-17, Charon 08d7c9d50144bd84848212c24701253585e90d1f, Aeneas be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a, Lean 4.35.0. The union of the thirty-two callable roots plus the original blanket-impl metadata root is extracted once into one Generated module and proved in one Proofs module.
limitations: Default delegation is a value-model contract, not verification of the actual supplied Default implementation or of its value/termination/effects. Discarded Rust payload destructors can panic, fail to terminate or affect external state; their execution and unwind/return ordering are not modeled. The Default success/failure/divergence statements must not be read as a claim covering all such Rust Drop behavior. For IntoEither::into_either_with the remaining premise is normal modeled predicate behavior on the actual argument; its original conversion dispatch has been proved from the real blanket instance. This does not establish interior-mutability or external captured-state effects beyond the value/reference model. Callback termination, panic freedom, captured-state effects and concrete closure correctness are not established by these conditional composition proofs. The theorem hypotheses describe modeled FnOnce results; unchanged modeled failure propagation does not specify Rust panic payloads, unwinding or external effects. Only the thirty-two named methods and the two-flip composition are proved. Other inherent and callback-taking APIs, iterators, pinning, standard trait implementations and serde remain unproved. Rust destructor behavior and resource consumption are outside the pure value model. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.
tool_limitations: Lean backend only, requiring cargo-proofs 0.4.0 or later. The version identifies the official Aeneas Git revision pinned in lake-manifest.json (backends/lean); this revision uses Lean 4.35.0. The recorder checks committed Lean theorem declarations and permits only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as transitive axioms. It rejects sorryAx and custom axioms, including axiomatized external models. Charon/Aeneas extraction is not rerun. The author must review that the committed functional model matches the recorded Rust source, that the named theorem corresponds to the public API, and that the reported precondition matches the theorem. A checked theorem alone does not establish those links or the adequacy of the specification. The current adapter records the default Cargo configuration, with ordinary Lean module paths and a pinned official Git dependency. Other backends, custom Lake source directories, and local-path Aeneas dependencies are unsupported.
